description: Mine radon (Rn-222) released by ventilation per tonne of coal mined, default for all countries without own factor
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Centre = China typical 9.3e5 Bq/t (S0001 Table 26, para 101; =2.8 TBq/GWa at 3.0e6 t/GWa); high = China small mines 3.5e6; low = 1980s crude 36 GBq/GWa (S0008 para 178) / 3.0e6 t/GWa = 1.2e4 (the other crude figure, 600 GBq/GWa = 2.0e5, lies inside). Only China was measured; use for every other country and for 1800-1949 is extrapolation (mining depth, gas content and ventilation differ). Engine rule: a country-specific row (e.g. CHN) overrides the XWL row. Not exhalation from residues.

description: Radium-226 released in coal mine drainage per tonne of coal mined, Poland (Upper Silesian balance)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Release to rivers 400 (1987), 219 (1995), 120 (2003), 77 (2006) MBq/d (S0222; S0225 gives 225 for 1995) divided by Polish production of those years from data/activity coal_production_t POL (S0804, whole country incl. lignite, so per-tonne values are diluted by about 25-30% against Silesian hard coal; applied to POL they reproduce the measured Bq/a). Low/high = observed spread of the four anchor years (falling with treatment); centre by the geometric-mean rule. No pre-1985 data and no other country: no row (gap). REVISION D59 (Steve, 2026-10-27): NO numeric change. FLAG: the high (548.8 Bq/t, the 1987 anchor of 400 MBq/d attributed to Ra-226 by S0222) may be 2-3x too high pending an S0222 check: S0251 (Michalik 2005 S505) says "by 1987 up to 400 MBq per day both isotopes", which could be the sum of the two isotopes (Ra-226 about 150 MBq/d). S0251 peak release 225 MBq/d Ra-226 is consistent with the 1995 anchor. Inflow 650 MBq/d (S0251 S504) is the stable anchor.

description: Fraction of mobilised Ra-226 retained underground in Polish coal mines (precipitated deposits and sludge)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. CONFLICT (S0222 over 70% retained; S0225 about 40%) resolved as time and treatment effect (D59). Pre-D59 bounds 0.4/0.55/0.7. Engine: retained = released x r/(1-r) using the Ra-226 drainage factor coal:0003 (formula is the stream spec's to confirm). Observation: S0222 balance (inflow about 650 vs 400 MBq/d released in 1987 = 38% retained; 77 in 2006 = 88%) suggests the two figures may be different years of improving treatment rather than a true source conflict. Tier set to impounded (coal_mining has no reisolated tier); REVISION D59 (Steve, 2026-10-27): high 0.7 -> 0.88. S0251 (Michalik 2005) inflow 650 MBq/d Ra-226: retention 1 - release/inflow = 0.65 at the peak release (225 MBq/d) to 0.88 in 2006 (77 MBq/d); S0251 text "nowadays up to 80%". Centre 0.55 kept. Caution: retained = released x r/(1-r) amplifies strongly at high r (0.55 -> 1.22; 0.88 -> 7.3); inflow minus release is the stable anchor (S0251; for the stream spec).

description: Ash-borne activity per tonne of fly ash from coal burned for power, U238+

description: Fraction of power-station ash escaping the stack, global average 1800-1949
notes: Unit-1 fraction of TOTAL power ash (the basis of the sources: UK 0.4% of all ash), applied to the ash-borne Bq of each group, multiplied by the group enrichment factor and capped so that released Bq never exceed the fly-ash Bq (engine). Release is subtracted from the coal_fly_ash quantity. JUDGEMENT, NO SOURCE for the centre 0.25. High 0.80 = whole fly-ash fraction escaping (maximum fly fraction in the activity builder, N100). No/limited control: fly-ash fraction of ash 0.3-0.65 (activity N100) x (1 - collector efficiency 20-90%, S0208 settling chamber 20-50%, multicyclone 75-90%). Centre 0.25 is a judgement (fly fraction about 0.45 x 0.55 escaping) not a published figure. Global era average over very different fleets; weak. REVISION D59 (Steve, 2026-10-27): numbers unchanged. High 0.80 now has a direct anchor: an uncontrolled plant discharges about 80% of the ash (Eisenbud and Petrow 1964, S0238 p.288). The centre 0.25 remains JUDGEMENT, NO SOURCE; no pre-1950 plant data exist in any paper.

description: Share of US power-station ash (fly, bottom, boiler slag) to impounded: landfill, ash pond and dyke (the unused remainder)
notes: REVISION D73 (Steve, 2026-11-06): NEW ROW. Replaces coal:0074-0079 (RETIRED D73). Region USA (ACAA basis). INERT while the ash drivers exist for XWL only (COAL_SPEC section 5 step 3); usable if per-country ash is added (option C, not decided). Fly ash + bottom ash + boiler slag combined, from the yearly ACAA survey sheets 1966-2024 (S0255-S0258; series in research/coal/acaa_series.csv and acaa_uses.csv; method research/coal/acaa_notes.md sections 4 and 6.2). Mapping of ACAA uses: L = all ACAA use; S1 = L less waste stabilisation, CCR pond closure, mining applications and oil/gas field services; S2 = S1 less structural fills. Dispersed central = S1 production-weighted over the era years with category detail, low = lowest annual S2, high = highest annual L. Reisolated = mining applications as a share of production (ACAA does not separate underground from surface placement, so an upper bound for underground), low 0, high = highest annual value. Centrals are stored to 3 decimals (dispersed = S1 pooled over detail years, reisolated = mining share, both rounded to 0.001) and impounded central = 1 - dispersed - reisolated, so the three centrals sum to exactly 1.000; impounded low = 1 - dispersed high - reisolated high, high = 1 - dispersed low. Bounds combine year-to-year variation, mapping choice and survey extrapolation (respondent coverage 30-68%); no extra margin for extrapolation (ACAA states none). Fly and bottom ash share one value although their use differs from 2015 on (2024: 78% vs 35%). FGD gypsum and FBC ash excluded. Not a world value. Era basis: 1966-1989: L mapping only (no use-category detail was read before 1990); fly + bottom + slag used 12-28% (S0255, S0256; 1987-89 S0257); dispersed low lowered by 0.03 for undetected disposal-like uses; reisolated 0.003 (high 0.02) is a placeholder (no category data).
